statement_summary: Security Officer and Privacy Officer designated in writing
Annual risk analysis with SP 800-30; risks owned and treated
Risk acceptance authority; High risks and patient-safety or controlled substance risks never accepted
HIPAA sanctions recorded; handbook points to the rule; good-faith reporting protected
No BAA, no ePHI, including free apps and equipment vendors; MSP subcontractor BAAs checked yearly
Annual independent evaluation
Six-year retention of security documentation; 2-year controlled substance records
Annual policy review; policies available to staff
Written, risk-rated, time-limited exceptions
EPCS audit report obtained and determination recorded before use and for each new report
Unique accounts in every system, including desktops and packaging software
Role-based least privilege; only pharmacists may annotate or alter controlled substance records
MFA for the suite, PMS, and every administrator login including MSP-held logins; number matching
Termination checklist completed by the last day
Monthly account reconciliation; quarterly role and controlled substance permission check
10-minute device lock; 15-minute PMS timeout; sign in as yourself for each task
Emergency PMS administrator access
Named MSP and vendor accounts with MFA; packaging vendor sessions only on request and logged
Password rules; no saved passwords; unique local administrator passwords; yearly Wi-Fi change
CSOS private key used only by its holder; others obtain their own certificate
Minimum necessary look-ups only
No ePHI in personal accounts, unapproved apps, or public AI tools
Lock screens; never share passwords or MFA codes
Training at hire and yearly; phishing simulations; EPCS, PDMP, and CSOS module for pharmacists
Report suspected incidents at once
Signed policy acknowledgment
Ransomware and downtime runbook kept and printed
Report suspected incidents within 1 hour
Log every incident
Four-factor breach risk assessment; discovery date recorded
Meet notification deadlines in the P08 matrix
Daily EPCS audit report review; one-business-day report to the PMS vendor and DEA
Stop and resume EPCS processing on vendor non-compliance notice
CSOS revocation request within 24 hours of substantiated compromise
Controlled substance theft or significant loss reported to the sheriff and DEA
PDMP reporting kept current during downtime
Insurer hotline first; MSP engaged under BAA
Ransom payment only with approvals and OFAC check
Business associate incident reports logged and handled
Annual tabletop exercise with the MSP and both pharmacists
Lessons learned within 30 days
Three classification levels
Encrypt Restricted data at rest and in transit, including email to the ALFs
Restricted data only in approved systems; weekly download clean-up
Device and ePHI inventory
New tools approved and under BAA before receiving Restricted data
Approved AI tools only; vendor-enabled decision support features reviewed before use
90-day immutable backup versions; quarterly restore test
Wipe or certified destruction with records; shred paper PHI
Retention of prescription, controlled substance, and security records
